page.layout: One printed page, one column of dictionary entries in Hebrew and Latin, with no marginal notes. Running head centred at top. Page number top right. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: גָּדוֹל m. Magnus, Magnificus, Psal.21.6. Constr. גְּדוֹל הָעֵצָה Maximus consilio, Jer.32.19. גְּדַל־חָסֶד Magnus benignitate, Psal.145.8. Aff. עַד גְּדוֹלִים usq; ad maximum eorum, Jer.6.13. Plur. גְּדוֹלִים Magni, Magnates, 1.Sam.17.v.14. Constr. אֶת־גְּדוֹלֵי הָעִיר Magnates civitatis istius, 2.Reg.10.6. Aff. גְּדוֹלָיו Magnates ejus, 2.Reg.10.11. Fœm. גְּדוֹלָה Magna, Gen.27.34. Plur. גְּדֹלוֹת, Psal.12.4.

גָּדֵל m. Magnus: & participialiter, Crescens, ut Gen.26.v.13. הָלוֹךְ וְגָדֵל Iens & crescens erat, id est, pergebat indesinenter crescere, 1.Sam.2.26. Plural. Constr. גְּדֵלֵי בָשָׂר Magni carne, Exod.16.26.
גֶּדֶל m. Magnitudo, Deut.32.3. Aff. וְאֶת־גָּדְלוֹ Et magnitudinem ejus, Deut.5.24. vel גְּדֻלּוֹ Psal.150.2.
גְּדֻלָּה f. Magnitudo, Magnificentia, Amplitudo, Esth.6.3. Constr. גְּדֻלַּת Esth.10.2. Aff. וּלְגָדְלָתוֹ Et amplitudinis ejus, Psal.145.3. Plural. גְּדֻלּוֹת Amplitudinum, 1.Par.17.12.

גְּדִלִים m.p. Institae, Deut.22.12. Fasciae, 1.Reg.7.17. Ex significatione Chaldaica, qua גָּדַל Intorquere, Implicare: תָּכָא דִּמְגַדְּלָא Catena quae contorta est, Eccles.4.12. גְּדִילָא Funis contortus, Jesa.5.18. & alibi. Apud Rabbinos, אִשָּׁה גּוֹדֶלֶת מְגַדְּלָא יִשְׂעַר Mulier implicans capillos: נְשִׂיָא Plicans crines mulierum, Zöpfe machen. גְּדִילִים Fila contorduplicata. Hinc ad Fasciās transfertur, quarum quasi Funibus constringunt.

מִגְדָּל m. Turris, Jes.5.2. Constr. מִגְדַּל, Jud.8.17. Plur. מִגְדָּלִים Turres, Jes.30.25. Aff. מִגְדָּלֶיהָ Turres ejus, Jes.26.v.4. Et fœm. מִגְדָּלוֹת Turres, 2.Par.32.5. Et aliâ significatione, מִגְדָּלוֹת Crescentes plantulæ, Flores, Cant.5.13. Quidam tamen in prima significatione accipiunt, pro Turriculis: Aff. בְּמִגְדְּלוֹתֶיךָ In turribus tuis, Ezech.27.11.

page.notes: Vowel points and some Hebrew letters in the Rabbinic line (מְגַדְּלָא יִשְׂעַר, נְשִׂיָא) are only roughly legible at this scan resolution; the consonants are reliable, the vowels are not verified. "Iens" in the second entry is printed as an I/J-form, read here as Jens-like; the Latin word is likely "Ibat". The Hebrew catchword at the bottom right is the next entry's headword.
